summary.plain: A giant balloon of clear liquid inside a mine in Japan, watched by nearly 1,900 light sensors, that catches antineutrinos from nuclear reactors across the country. A xenon-loaded inner balloon suspended at its centre (KamLAND-Zen) uses the same detector to search for a different rare process.
summary.technical: ~1000 t liquid-scintillator antineutrino detector in an 18 m diameter vessel with 1,879 PMTs, surrounded by a water-Cherenkov muon veto, in the old Kamiokande cavity of the Kamioka mine; operating since 2002-01-17.

technology.note: Detailed structural description (containment vessel dimensions, PMT count, veto mass) sourced only from Wikipedia (rank 12) this session; no official/paper source was independently fetched to corroborate these exact figures, so confidence is kept approximate. This record is referenced by the neutrino-mass-0vbb workstream for KamLAND-Zen (which reuses this same detector volume with a different central balloon/isotope load); the placement/site below is the load-bearing fact for that reference and is sourced accordingly.
technology.quote: an 18-meter-diameter stainless steel containment vessel lined with 1,879 photomultiplier tubes, surrounded by a 3.2 kiloton cylindrical water Cherenkov detector for cosmic ray shielding
technology.value: Liquid-scintillator antineutrino detector: an 18-m-diameter spherical balloon of liquid scintillator viewed by photomultiplier tubes, surrounded by a mineral-oil buffer and an outer water-Cherenkov muon veto
